notes.subject: car
notes.text: Big visible car that is either red or white; each version has its own island.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Short plates in a bright blue or dark blue design.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: A blend of Renaissance, Baroque, Rococo and Victorian influences, with big arches, plazas and courtyards.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Some streets and places keep colonial-era Scandinavian names such as 'gade', and there are bilingual signs in older downtown areas.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: An American overseas territory, counted as the mainland country for streaks.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Red truck with red cab is found only on the southern island of St Croix, and is the commonest car there.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A white car with no antenna also appears on St Croix, less often than the red one.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: White car with an antenna and a shorter cab is only on St Thomas and St John.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: On St Croix main roads form a loose grid, running WSW to ENE and crossed NNW to SSE.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: St Thomas and St John have much curvier roads than St Croix.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Two boat trekkers on St Croix's north coast show blue water and hilly islands, with a pink tint near Buck Island.
